newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa tumbles to new seven-month lows.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa tumbles to new seven-month lows.

text.p: London cocoa futures took a new plunge to seven-month lows late on Tuesday as sellers knocked prices down after disappointment over the market's recent performance.
"There were small periods of panic. The market lost eight pounds and then stopped, then lost more," said one trader.
Pressure came from speculative shorts, as well as disappointed longs and origins. But a good two-way trade developed after benchmark March cocoa slipped below 930 stg.
Traders said the latest pounding cleared the way for a test of 910 and subsequently 880, technical support points derived from extrapolating a downtrend channel in place since October.
"I think we are now looking to go to 880," said one.
March cocoa skidded to a session low of 923 stg, ending just off the lows at 925 stg a tonne. The close is a new contract low.
Traders said E.D. & F. Man had been a good seller on the March contract.
Spot December lost 13 stg to 892 after a low of 890.
Tuesday's total volume of 5,115 lots included a fair amount of switches and crosses. Dec/March was slightly firmer at 31-32 stg after early trades at 33-34 and March/May was at 17 from 18-19.
New York cocoa futures also suffered heavy losses in early dealings pressured by technically-inspired speculative and commission house selling. The March contract tumbled $30 to $1,353.
One trader said the arbitrage between London and New York was narrow at around 100-101 stg and there was room for widening.
On fundamental news, Ivorian arrivals are estimated to have exceeded 100,000 tonnes since the opening of the new season, with stocks at Abidjan alone believed to be over 100,000 tonnes.
Exporters are expecting arrivals to take off from the middle of November.
